passage:
An earthquake museum was built in a town that had once been badly damaged. It showed broken walls, rescue tools, survivor stories, and building safety lessons.
Students expected a frightening visit. Some parts were sad, but much of the museum focused on preparation and rebuilding.
A survivor told them that memory should not only hurt. It should teach.
After the visit, students checked whether heavy furniture at home was fixed to walls.
The museum turned disaster into responsibility. It did not let people forget fear, but it also did not leave them helpless.
Remembering danger can become a way to protect the future.
